videos.script:
So far the planner's tokens and components live inside the planner. The day a second app needs them, somebody copies the folder. And from that day, there are two design systems.

{{package}} This lesson turns them into a package. A folder with a name, a version, and a list of what it exports. You will build it with Vite's library mode, and look inside the file npm would publish.

{{semver}} Then the version number, and the promise each of its three parts makes. For a design system, renaming a token is a breaking change, even though nothing fails to compile.

{{registry}} Then a registry of your own. Verdaccio runs on your computer and speaks the same protocol as npm. You log in, you publish, and the planner installs its own components from it, with every test still green.

{{release}} And a second release. A new component, a changelog entry, a minor version. And the planner, told by npm that it is one version behind.
